scope: independent process-local monkeypatch; exact root actuator harness and synthetic model inputs; no production source changes/ROS2/vehicle
source_hash_limit: production planner hashes match frozen benchmarks; root added metric classification in its harness during research; per-trace hashes preserve outputs, timing runs included concurrent offline workers
production_decision: reject horizon/desired-speed/early-side-guide changes: original 5m head-on remains a physical oracle collision with all hard guards intact
conclusions: No tested lightweight variant solves the 5m known-CV0.7m/s head-on case
Longer nominal/parking horizon is conservative without a richer nonconstant control sequence
A safe present finite braking rollout is not a recursively safe backup or an invariant refuge against a noncooperative moving target
Zero trap/mode switches in all tested encounters; keep dynamic yielding separate from mechanical recovery
Full desired-speed setpoints broaden future acceleration expressiveness but need whole-interface safety verification and did not solve this counterexample
